questions.question: Does $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{WKL}_0$ over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$? Does $\mathsf{RT}^2_{<\infty}$?
questions.context: Seetapun [@seetapunslaman1995] showed that RT²₂ admits cone avoidance, so RT²₂ does not imply ACA₀. Whether it implies the much weaker WKL₀ — equivalently, whether every instance can be solved without computing a PA degree — remained open until Liu [@liu2012] proved PA avoidance for RT²₂. Since ω-models of RT²₂ are models of RT²_{<∞}, the second part follows.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$ (equivalently, $\mathsf{COH}$)? Does $\mathsf{SRT}^2_{<\infty}$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_{<\infty}$ (equivalently, $\mathsf{COH}$)?
questions.context: Cholak, Jockusch and Slaman [@cholakjockuschslaman2001] decomposed RT²₂ into its stable part SRT²₂ and its cohesive part COH, and asked whether the stable part alone suffices. This became one of the central questions of the field. Chong, Slaman and Yang [@chongslamanyang2014] gave a negative answer using a non-standard model in which every set is low; the question for ω-models — that is, for computability theory proper — was answered negatively by Monin and Patey [@moninpatey2021].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2$? Does $\mathsf{RT}^2_{<\infty}$ imply $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_3$?
questions.context: RT²₂ implies BΣ⁰₂ [@hirst1987] and is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + IΣ⁰₂ [@cholakjockuschslaman2001], so its first-order part lies between BΣ⁰₂ and IΣ⁰₂. Chong, Slaman and Yang [@chongslamanyang2017] showed that it does not reach IΣ⁰₂; Slaman and Yokoyama [@slamanyokoyama2018] answered the question for arbitrarily many colors.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{RT}^2_2$ $\Pi^0_2$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$? In particular, does it prove the totality of the Ackermann function, or the consistency of $\mathsf{I}\Sigma_1$? Does it prove that $\omega^\omega$ is well-ordered?
questions.answer: Yes. RT²₂ (even with WKL₀) is ∀Π⁰₃-conservative over RCA₀, so it proves no new Π⁰₂ sentence; nor does it prove that ω^ω is well-ordered.
questions.context: This asks whether RT²₂ is "finitistically reducible": whether the Π⁰₂ consequences of RT²₂, which correspond to provably total functions, are already those of IΣ⁰₁ (primitive recursive functions). Patey and Yokoyama [@pateyyokoyama2018] answered positively by a model-theoretic argument based on a new notion of largeness of finite sets.

questions.question: Does every $\Delta^0_2$ set have an infinite low subset in it or in its complement? Equivalently, does every computable stable coloring of pairs have an infinite low homogeneous set?
questions.answer: No — there is a Δ⁰₂ set with no infinite low subset in either it or its complement.
questions.context: A relativizable positive answer would have separated SRT²₂ from RT²₂, since RT²₂ has computable instances without low₂ solutions [@jockusch1972]. The answer is negative [@downeyetal2001], which is why the separation of SRT²₂ from RT²₂ needed other ideas: Chong, Slaman and Yang [@chongslamanyang2014] built a non-standard model in which every set is low.

questions.question: For every 2-coloring $C$ of $[\mathbb{N}]^2$ which is not of PA degree, is there an infinite homogeneous set $H$ such that $C \oplus H$ is not of PA degree?
questions.context: A relativizable positive answer gives an ω-model of RT²₂ with no PA degree, hence separates RT²₂ from WKL₀ (see the question on RT²₂ and WKL₀). Liu [@liu2012] proved it with a new forcing notion whose conditions are Mathias conditions with a Π⁰₁ class of reservoirs.

questions.question: Does the chain/antichain principle $\mathsf{CAC}$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$?
questions.context: CAC follows easily from RT²₂ by coloring pairs according to comparability. Hirschfeldt and Shore [@hirschfeldtshore2007] showed that CAC is much weaker: it has an ω-model with no DNR function, while RT²₂ implies DNR.

questions.question: Does the free set theorem $\mathsf{FS}^2$, or the thin set theorem $\mathsf{TS}^2$, imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$? Does $\mathsf{FS}^2 + \mathsf{WKL}_0$? Does $\mathsf{FS}^2$ imply $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: The free set and thin set theorems [@cholaketal2005] are consequences of Ramsey's theorem in which the homogeneity requirement is weakened. They are natural candidates for principles strictly between RCA₀ and RT²₂.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{FS}^2 + \mathsf{CAC}$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$? Does $\mathsf{FS}^2 + \mathsf{COH}$?
questions.context: Combining a free set principle with a principle handling the "unstable" part of colorings is a natural attempt to recover RT²₂, by analogy with RT²₂ ⇔ SRT²₂ + COH [@cholakjockuschslaman2001].

questions.question: Do the free set or thin set theorems for exponent $k \ge 3$, or for all exponents, imply $\mathsf{ACA}_0$?
questions.context: Ramsey's theorem for triples implies ACA₀ [@jockusch1972], unlike RT²₂. Whether the weaker free set and thin set theorems behave like Ramsey's theorem for pairs at every exponent was settled by Wang [@wang2014b], who showed that they admit strong cone avoidance at every exponent.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{SADS}$ imply $\mathsf{SCAC}$?
questions.context: Hirschfeldt and Shore [@hirschfeldtshore2007] introduced the stable versions of ADS and CAC and showed that SCAC implies SADS.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{CRT}^2_2$, or even $\mathsf{CADS}$, imply $\mathsf{COH}$?
questions.context: COH implies both CADS and the cohesive Ramsey theorem CRT²₂ [@hirschfeldtshore2007]. Over ω-models, and even for Weihrauch reducibility, CADS is equivalent to COH [@fioricaronesshafersolda2022], and CADS implies COH over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂ [@dzhafarovmummert2022]; so a negative answer over RCA₀ would have to use non-standard models.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{CADS}$ imply $\mathsf{CRT}^2_2$?
questions.context: A companion of the question whether CADS implies COH: CRT²₂ lies between COH and CADS [@hirschfeldtshore2007].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{SADS}$, or even $\mathsf{PART}$, imply $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: SCAC implies BΣ⁰₂ [@hirschfeldtshore2007], and the question asks how far down this goes. Chong, Lempp and Yang [@chonglemppyang2010] showed that PART, and hence SADS, implies BΣ⁰₂.

questions.question: Are the principles weaker than $\mathsf{ACA}_0$ studied by Hirschfeldt and Shore (other than those following from $\mathsf{WKL}_0$ or $\mathsf{COH}$) $\Pi^1_1$-conservative, or at least arithmetically conservative, over $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.answer: COH, ADS, CAC and their stable versions are Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂.
questions.context: Proving conservation over BΣ⁰₂ is harder than over IΣ⁰₂, since the usual forcing arguments use Σ⁰₂-induction. Chong, Slaman and Yang [@chongslamanyang2012] developed techniques for models of BΣ⁰₂ and showed conservation for the main principles weaker than RT²₂.

questions.question: Is there an exponent $n$ such that the rainbow Ramsey theorem $\mathsf{RRT}^n_2$ implies $\mathsf{ACA}_0$?
questions.context: Ramsey's theorem RTⁿ₂ implies ACA₀ for every n ≥ 3, but the rainbow Ramsey theorem is much weaker: Csima and Mileti [@csimamileti2009] showed RRT²₂ follows from 2-randomness. Wang [@wang2013] showed that RRT³₂ does not imply ACA₀, and later that no exponent does [@wang2014b].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{IPT}^2_2$ (or $\mathsf{IPT}^2_2 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$) imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$? Does $\mathsf{IPT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$? Is $\mathsf{IPT}^2_2$ implied by $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ over ω-models? For arbitrarily many colors, does $\mathsf{SRT}^2_{<\infty}$ imply $\mathsf{IPT}^2_{<\infty}$, and does $\mathsf{IPT}^2_{<\infty}$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_{<\infty}$?
questions.context: The increasing polarized Ramsey theorem IPT²₂ [@dzhafarovhirst2009] lies between SRT²₂ and RT²₂. An equivalence between IPT²₂ + BΣ⁰₂ and RT²₂ would follow from SRT²₂ ⇒ RT²₂, so separating them is at least as hard as the SRT²₂ vs. RT²₂ question.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{SIPT}^2_2$ or $\mathsf{SPT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ (equivalently, $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$)?
questions.context: Dzhafarov and Hirst [@dzhafarovhirst2009] showed that the stable polarized principles together with BΣ⁰₂ imply SRT²₂. Chong, Lempp and Yang [@chonglemppyang2010] showed that they imply BΣ⁰₂ themselves.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{COH}$ (or $\mathsf{CADS}$) imply the atomic model theorem $\mathsf{AMT}$? Does $\mathsf{CADS}$ imply $\mathsf{OPT}$?
questions.context: Hirschfeldt, Shore and Slaman [@hirschfeldtshoreslaman2009] placed AMT below SADS and OPT (omitting partial types) below AMT. COH and CADS are the natural "unstable" principles to compare with them.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{AMT}$ imply $\overline{\mathsf{D}}_2\mathsf{IP}$? Does $\mathsf{OPT}$? Does $\overline{\mathsf{D}}_2\mathsf{IP}$ imply $\mathsf{FIP}$?
questions.context: Dzhafarov and Mummert [@dzhafarovmummert2013] studied intersection principles for families of sets. The principles D_nIP asking for a maximal subfamily with the D_n intersection property are equivalent to ACA₀; their weak versions D̄_nIP (written D_nIP in [@dzhafarovmummert2010] and nIP in [@cholakdowneyigusa2017]) form a hierarchy below the finite intersection principle FIP, close to the atomic model theorem. AMT implies D̄₂IP over RCA₀ + IΣ⁰₂.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{ASRAM}$ imply $\mathsf{SRAM}$? Does $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{ASRAM}$, or conversely? Does $\mathsf{ASRT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{WWKL}_0$?
questions.context: Dzhafarov [@dzhafarov2011] introduced the "almost" versions of stable Ramsey principles, inspired by the reverse mathematics of the sorites paradox.

questions.question: Unique choice on Baire space is Weihrauch-equivalent to closed choice on Baire space, $\mathsf{UC}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}} \equiv_W \mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}$.
questions.context: C_ℕ^ℕ and UC_ℕ^ℕ are the Weihrauch counterparts of ATR₀-like principles [@brattkadebrechtpauly2012]. The conjecture was refuted: unique choice is strictly weaker than closed choice on Baire space.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{DNR}$ imply the Ramsey-type weak König's lemma $\mathsf{RWKL}$?
questions.context: Flood [@flood2012] introduced RWKL, which asks for an infinite set homogeneous for a path of a binary tree, and showed that it is implied by SRT²₂ and implies DNR.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{D}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{P}^2_2$?
questions.context: A question from Flood's study of Ramsey-type versions of König's lemma [@flood2012].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{TT}^1$ prove $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: The tree theorem for singletons TT¹ (every finite coloring of the full binary tree has a monochromatic subtree isomorphic to it) is a tree analogue of the infinite pigeonhole principle, which is equivalent to BΣ⁰₂ [@hirst1987]. Its first-order strength was a natural question since the obvious proofs use more induction.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ or $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$ $\Pi^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.answer: RT²₂ + WKL₀ is ∀Π⁰₄-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂; full Π¹₁-conservation is open.
questions.context: RT²₂ implies BΣ⁰₂ and is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + IΣ⁰₂ [@cholakjockuschslaman2001], so the question is whether BΣ⁰₂ is exactly its first-order part. Le Houérou, Levy Patey and Yokoyama [@lehoueroupateyyokoyama2024] proved conservation for ∀Π⁰₄ sentences, which covers BΣ⁰₂ itself and the consistency statements usually considered.

questions.question: Does the thin set theorem $\mathsf{TS}^2$ imply $\mathsf{RRT}^2_2$?
questions.context: Both are consequences of RT²₂ obtained by weakening homogeneity [@cholaketal2005] [@csimamileti2009].

questions.question: Does the Ramsey-type 2-coloring principle $\mathsf{RCOLOR}_2$ imply $\mathsf{DNR}$? Does it imply $\mathsf{RWKL}$?
questions.context: Ramsey-type versions of graph coloring ask for an infinite set of vertices that can be monochromatic in some coloring. For k ≥ 3 colors they are all equivalent to RWKL [@bienvenupateyshafer2017], which implies DNR; the case of two colors behaves differently.

questions.question: Is there a $\Delta^0_2$ set such that every infinite subset of it or of its complement has a jump of PA degree relative to $\emptyset'$?
questions.answer: No — every Δ⁰₂ set has an infinite subset in it or its complement whose jump is not PA over ∅′.
questions.context: A set computes solutions to all computable instances of COH exactly when its jump is PA over ∅′ [@jockuschstephan1993]. A positive answer would therefore have shown that SRT²₂ implies COH in ω-models; the negative answer of Monin and Patey [@moninpatey2021] is the core of their separation of SRT²₂ from RT²₂ in ω-models.

questions.question: Does the Erdős–Moser theorem $\mathsf{EM}$ imply $\mathsf{COH}$? Does it imply $\mathsf{1}\text{-}\mathsf{GEN}$?
questions.context: EM and ADS together are equivalent to RT²₂ [@bovykinweiermann2017], and ADS implies COH. Since COH is the "unstable" part of RT²₂, whether EM alone already captures it is a natural question.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{COH}$ generalized uniformly reducible to $\mathsf{SRT}^2_{<\infty}$? Is $\mathsf{COH}$ strongly computably reducible to $\mathsf{SRT}^2_k$ for $k > 2$, or to $\mathsf{SRT}^2_{<\infty}$?
questions.context: Dzhafarov [@dzhafarov2016] showed that COH is not strongly computably reducible to SRT²₂, a first step toward separating the two principles; these questions ask how far that separation extends.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{WWKL}$ strongly computably reducible to $\mathsf{RT}^n_k$ for $n \ge 3$, or to $\mathsf{RT}$?
questions.context: Over ω-models, RTⁿₖ for n ≥ 3 is equivalent to ACA₀ and so implies WWKL. Strong computable reducibility forbids using the instance itself, and Hirschfeldt and Jockusch [@hirschfeldtjockusch2016] asked whether this matters.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{TS}^2$ imply $\mathsf{FS}^2$? Do $\mathsf{FS}^2$ or $\mathsf{TS}^2$ imply $\mathsf{EM}$?
questions.context: FS² implies TS² [@cholaketal2005]. Since RT²₂ ⇔ EM + ADS [@bovykinweiermann2017], comparing the free and thin set theorems with EM is a way to understand which part of RT²₂ they capture.

questions.question: Does the tree theorem for pairs $\mathsf{TT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{ACA}_0$? Does it admit cone avoidance?
questions.context: TT²₂ strengthens RT²₂ by coloring pairs of comparable nodes of the binary tree. Seetapun's cone avoidance argument for RT²₂ [@seetapunslaman1995] does not adapt directly because of the disjoint extension commitments of the tree structure.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{SRRT}^2_2 + \mathsf{COH}$ imply $\mathsf{RRT}^2_2$?
questions.context: The analogue for the rainbow Ramsey theorem of the decomposition RT²₂ ⇔ SRT²₂ + COH [@cholakjockuschslaman2001].

questions.question: Both $\mathsf{COH}$ and $\mathsf{EM}$ admit preservation of the arithmetic hierarchy.
questions.context: Wang [@wang2016] introduced preservation of the arithmetic hierarchy to separate principles by their definability strength, and showed that WKL and RRT²₂ have it. Patey [@patey2015d] proved the conjecture for COH and EM.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{2}\text{-}\mathsf{RWWKL}$ imply $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: The Ramsey-type weak weak König's lemma relative to ∅′ is a consequence of 2-WWKL, which implies BΣ⁰₂ [@avigaddeanrute2012].

questions.question: Is the intermediate value theorem Weihrauch reducible to $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$?
questions.context: In the Weihrauch lattice, Ramsey's theorem for pairs cannot be reduced to PA, MLR or COH for reasons of Borel measurability [@brattkarakotoniaina2017], but which problems of analysis lie below it is less clear. IVT is a natural candidate: it is below WKL and computably true.

questions.question: How do the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^2_2$ and the Erdős–Rado theorem for the rationals $\mathsf{ER}^2_2$ compare? Does $\mathsf{ER}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{ACA}_0$? Does $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{ER}^2_2$?
questions.context: Both strengthen RT²₂ by adding structure to the homogeneous set: a copy of the full binary tree for TT²₂, a dense subset of the rationals for ER²₂ (written η → (ℵ₀, η)² in some papers). Seetapun's argument fails for both because of "disjoint extension commitments" [@frittaionpatey2017]; Dzhafarov and Patey [@dzhafarovpatey2017] overcame it for TT²₂, while ER²₂ only has half of this difficulty yet remains unsettled.

questions.question: Does the Erdős–Rado theorem for singletons $\mathsf{ER}^1$ imply $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: ER¹ (every finite coloring of the rationals has a dense monochromatic subset on some interval) and the tree theorem TT¹ have the same state of the art: both are provable in RCA₀ + IΣ⁰₂ and strictly stronger than BΣ⁰₂ [@frittaionpatey2017].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{TT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{WKL}_0$? Does the stable tree theorem $\mathsf{STT}^2_2$ imply the cohesive one $\mathsf{CTT}^2_2$, or $\mathsf{COH}$, at least over ω-models? Does $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{CTT}^2_2$ in ω-models?
questions.context: The tree theorem decomposes, like RT²₂, into stable and cohesive parts. These are tree analogues of the SRT²₂ vs. COH question; since SRT²₂ does not imply COH in ω-models [@moninpatey2021], the analogous question for trees is expected to have the same answer.

questions.question: Does the variable word theorem $\mathsf{VW}(2,2)$, or its ordered version $\mathsf{OVW}(2,2)$, imply $\mathsf{ACA}_0$?
questions.context: Variable word theorems come from the Hales–Jewett theorem. Their upper bound in the reverse mathematics hierarchy was unknown: the usual proofs go through Hindman-type arguments.

questions.question: Is the grouping principle $\mathsf{GP}^2_2$ $\Pi^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$? Does $\mathsf{EM}$ imply $\mathsf{GP}^2_2$?
questions.context: Patey and Yokoyama [@pateyyokoyama2018] introduced the grouping principle to obtain density bounds for the Erdős–Moser theorem in their conservation proof for RT²₂. Le Houérou, Levy Patey and Yokoyama [@lehoueroupateyyokoyama2024] later showed GP²₂ + WKL₀ Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{RRT}^2_2$ imply Hindman's theorem for sums of exactly two elements $\mathsf{HT}^{=2}_2$?
questions.context: Csima, Dzhafarov, Hirschfeldt, Jockusch, Solomon and Westrick [@csimaetal2019] showed that HT^{=2}_2 is computably much weaker than full Hindman's theorem but still not computably true; the rainbow Ramsey theorem is a natural comparison point.

questions.question: Where does Cousin's lemma for Baire class 1 functions fall in the reverse mathematics hierarchy?
questions.answer: It is equivalent to ACA₀ over RCA₀.
questions.context: Cousin's lemma (every gauge on [0,1] has a fine tagged partition) is equivalent to Π¹₁-CA₀ for arbitrary functions coded suitably, and Barrett [@barrett2020] gave a heuristic suggesting the same for Baire class 1 gauges. The answer turned out to be much lower: ACA₀ [@barrettdowneygreenberg2021].

questions.question: Over $\mathsf{RCA}_0^*$, does $\mathsf{RT}^2_2 + \mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_1$ imply $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: Over RCA₀, RT²₂ implies BΣ⁰₂ [@hirst1987]. Kołodziejczyk, Kowalik and Yokoyama [@koodziejczykkowalikyokoyama2020] studied Ramsey's theorem when only Δ⁰₁-induction is assumed, where RT²₂ alone does not even imply IΣ⁰₁; adding IΣ⁰₁ back is the natural intermediate case.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$ computably reducible to the polarized Ramsey theorem $\mathsf{PT}^2_2$?
questions.context: PT²₂ is equivalent to RT²₂ over RCA₀ [@dzhafarovhirst2009], but the proof of RT²₂ from PT²₂ uses the principle more than once, so the question is whether a single application suffices.

questions.question: Is Hindman's theorem $\mathsf{HT}$ provable in $\mathsf{ACA}_0$? Does it imply $\mathsf{ACA}_0^+$? Is there a computable instance of $\mathsf{HT}$ all of whose solutions compute $\emptyset''$?
questions.context: Blass, Hirst and Simpson [@blasshirstsimpson1987] showed that Hindman's theorem is provable in ACA₀⁺ and implies ACA₀, and this gap has remained one of the most famous open problems of reverse mathematics. Every computable instance has a Δ⁰₄ solution, while some computable instance has no Δ⁰₂ solution; closing the gap would need either a new proof of Hindman's theorem or a coding of the double jump.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{RRT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{TAC}$?
questions.context: TAC, the chain/antichain principle for trees (every infinite subtree of ℕ^{<ℕ} has an infinite path or an infinite antichain) [@cervellegaudelierpatey2022], and RRT²₂ are both principles strictly below ACA₀ that do not follow from WKL₀.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{1}\text{-}\mathsf{GEN}$ Weihrauch reducible to the finite intersection principle $\mathsf{FIP}$?
questions.context: FIP is equivalent to 1-GEN over RCA₀ [@dzhafarovmummert2022]; the question asks whether the equivalence is uniform.

questions.question: Over $\mathsf{RCA}_0^*$, does $\mathsf{COH}$ imply $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_1$?
questions.context: Over RCA₀*, several consequences of RT²₂ such as RT²₂ itself, CAC and ADS do not imply IΣ⁰₁ [@fioricaroneskoodziejczykkowalik2021]. COH is the natural next candidate, since its usual proof iterates a construction along ℕ.

questions.question: Over $\mathsf{RCA}_0^*$, does $\mathsf{ADS}$ or $\mathsf{CAC}$ imply $\mathsf{CRT}^2_2$?
questions.context: Over RCA₀, ADS and CAC imply COH, hence CRT²₂, and BΣ⁰₂. Over RCA₀*, where only Δ⁰₁-induction is available, the usual proofs break down, and Kowalik [@kowalik2024] asked whether the implications survive.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{OVW}$ $\Pi^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: Le Houérou and Patey [@lehoueroupatey2024] proved that the ordered variable word theorem, together with WKL₀, is ∀Π⁰₄-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂, by the largeness techniques developed for RT²₂. Patey [@patey2026] obtained full Π¹₁-conservation by formalizing a weakly low basis theorem for OVW.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{WKL}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$ prove the bounded Ramsey theorem $\mathsf{BRT}^2_2$? Does $\mathsf{CAC}$?
questions.context: BRT²₂ follows from RT²₂, from EM [@lehoueroupatey2025] and from IΣ⁰₂, but not from BΣ⁰₂ alone nor from ADS. These questions ask whether compactness, or the chain/antichain principle, suffices.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{TT}^2_2$ $\Pi^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.answer: TT²₂ + WKL₀ is ∀Π⁰₄-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂; full Π¹₁-conservation is open.
questions.context: The analogue for the tree theorem of the long-standing question whether RT²₂ is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{RRT}^2_2$ imply the finite intersection principle $\mathsf{FIP}$? Does $\mathsf{COH}$? Over ω-models?
questions.context: FIP is equivalent to 1-GEN over RCA₀ [@dzhafarovmummert2022], so the question asks whether these principles produce sets that are generic enough.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{ADS}$ imply $\mathsf{CAC}$?
questions.context: Hirschfeldt and Shore [@hirschfeldtshore2007] showed that CAC implies ADS and that both are strictly weaker than RT²₂. Lerman, Solomon and Towsner [@lermansolomontowsner2013] separated them with an ω-model built by an iterated forcing construction, a method that became a standard tool for separating Ramsey-type principles.

questions.question: Is the Erdős–Moser theorem $\mathsf{EM}$ strictly weaker than $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$?
questions.context: RT²₂ implies EM, and EM together with ADS (or CAC) implies RT²₂ [@bovykinweiermann2017]. Lerman, Solomon and Towsner [@lermansolomontowsner2013] showed that EM does not even imply SRT²₂.

questions.question: Is the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^2_2$ strictly stronger than $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$? Does $\mathsf{TT}^2_2$ prove $\mathsf{TT}^2_{<\infty}$, or $\mathsf{RT}^2_{<\infty}$?
questions.context: For singletons, the tree theorem is strictly stronger than the pigeonhole principle (Corduan, Groszek and Mileti). For pairs, a positive answer to the second question would make TT²₂ strictly stronger than RT²₂, since RT²₂ does not prove RT²_{<∞} [@cholakjockuschslaman2001].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{WKL}_0$, or at least $\mathsf{WWKL}_0$?
questions.context: Kjos-Hanssen raised the question in the Banff problem list as "a major problem in reverse mathematics", together with questions about subsets of random sets. Liu answered both parts negatively, even for RT²₂: RT²₂ admits PA avoidance [@liu2012] and avoids all closed sets of measure zero [@liu2015].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{G}_\delta\text{-}\mathsf{REG}$ together with $\mathsf{WWKL}_0$ imply $\mathsf{RRT}^2_2$?
questions.context: Csima and Mileti [@csimamileti2009] showed that 2-randomness implies RRT²₂; the question asks whether weaker measure-theoretic principles suffice.

questions.question: The strong Tietze extension theorem (for functions with moduli of uniform continuity) is equivalent to $\mathsf{WKL}_0$ over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$.
questions.context: Giusto and Simpson [@giustosimpson2000] studied located sets in reverse mathematics and conjectured the equivalence; Shafer [@shafer2016] proved it for several versions of the theorem.

questions.question: How strong is the statement that if $\alpha$ is well-ordered and $Q$ is a wqo, then the $\alpha$-sequences over $Q$ with finite range form a wqo?
questions.answer: It is equivalent to ATR₀ over RCA₀.
questions.context: This is Nash-Williams' generalization of Higman's lemma to transfinite sequences with finite range. Montalbán expected the answer to come from an analysis of the maximal order types of the wqos involved. Pakhomov and Soldà [@pakhomovsolda2024] proved it in ATR₀, giving the equivalence.

questions.question: Is Nash-Williams' theorem — if $Q$ is a bqo, then so is the set of transfinite sequences over $Q$ — equivalent to $\mathsf{ATR}_0$?
questions.context: Marcone [@marcone1994] showed that the theorem is provable in Π¹₁-CA₀ but not equivalent to it, and Shore's work [@shore1993] shows that it implies ATR₀. Over ATR₀ it is equivalent to the generalized Higman theorem (if Q is a bqo, so is Q^{<ω}). The finite-range version for wqos is now known to be equivalent to ATR₀ [@pakhomovsolda2024], but the bqo version remains open.

questions.question: Is Fraïssé's conjecture (Laver's theorem: countable linear orders are well-quasi-ordered under embeddability) equivalent to $\mathsf{ATR}_0$? Is it even provable in $\Pi^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{CA}_0$?
questions.answer: It is provable in Π¹₁-CA₀, even in a weaker pseudo-Π¹₁-comprehension principle; whether it is equivalent to ATR₀ is open.
questions.context: Shore [@shore1993] showed that Fraïssé's conjecture implies ATR₀, and in fact that its restriction to well-orders is equivalent to ATR₀. Laver's proof uses bqo theory far beyond ATR₀. A negative answer would give a new robust subsystem of second-order arithmetic, since the conjecture is equivalent to many statements about the structure of linear orders under embeddability.

questions.question: Is there a system weaker than $\mathsf{ATR}_0$ that proves that the antichain $\mathbf{3}$ with three elements is a bqo? Does "$\mathbf{3}$ is a bqo" imply $\mathsf{ATR}_0$?
questions.context: RCA₀ proves that 2 is a bqo, and for every n ≥ 3 that if n is a bqo then so is n+1; but the only known proof that 3 is a bqo uses the clopen Ramsey theorem, equivalent to ATR₀. Freund [@freund2022b] made the first progress from below: "3 is a bqo" implies ACA₀⁺, and its Δ⁰₂ version implies ATR₀.

questions.question: Is the Auslander–Ellis theorem of topological dynamics equivalent to $\mathsf{ACA}_0$?
questions.context: Blass, Hirst and Simpson [@blasshirstsimpson1987] proved the theorem in ACA₀⁺, in the same paper as Hindman's theorem, and Simpson conjectured both to be equivalent to ACA₀. Kreuzer [@kreuzer2013] related it to minimal idempotent ultrafilters. The gap between ACA₀ and ACA₀⁺ remains open, as for Hindman's theorem.

questions.question: For all $2 \le k \le m$, the statement "every locally $k$-colorable graph is $m$-colorable" is equivalent to $\mathsf{WKL}_0$ over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$.
questions.context: A graph is locally k-colorable when each finite subgraph is k-colorable. By compactness it is then k-colorable, and Gasarch and Hirst [@gasarchhirst1994] showed that this is equivalent to WKL₀ for m = k. Their conjecture says that even the weak conclusion of m-colorability, for m much larger than k, already requires WKL₀. Schmerl [@schmerl2000] proved it.

questions.question: Is the problem of comparing well-orders by embeddings (WCWO) Weihrauch equivalent to unique choice on Baire space $\mathsf{UC}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}$?
questions.context: Kihara, Marcone and Pauly [@kiharamarconepauly2020] looked for a Weihrauch counterpart of ATR₀ among the problems equivalent to it in reverse mathematics. Weak comparability of well-orders was one candidate; Goh [@goh2020b] showed that it is equivalent to UC_ℕ^ℕ, the problem of computing a path through a tree with exactly one path.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{COH}$ omnisciently computably reducible to $\mathsf{RT}^1$, or to $\mathsf{D}^2_2$ or $\mathsf{D}^2_{<\infty}$?
questions.context: COH ≤_oc D²₂ means that for every COH instance there is a D²₂ instance all of whose solutions compute a solution to the COH instance, with no computability restriction on the D²₂ instance. Dzhafarov and Mummert [@dzhafarovmummert2022] call it "the distillation of the SRT²₂ vs. COH problem to its most combinatorial form". Monin and Patey [@moninpatey2021] separated SRT²₂ from COH in ω-models, which rules out computable reductions but not omniscient ones.

questions.question: Over $\mathsf{RCA}_0^*$, does $\mathsf{RT}^3_2$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^4_2$? More generally, does $\mathsf{RT}^n_2$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^{n+1}_2$ for some or all $n \ge 3$?
questions.context: Over RCA₀, RTⁿ₂ is equivalent to ACA₀ for every n ≥ 3 [@jockusch1972]. Over RCA₀*, where Σ⁰₁-induction may fail, Kołodziejczyk, Kowalik and Yokoyama [@koodziejczykkowalikyokoyama2020] studied what remains of this collapse when only Δ⁰₁-induction is available, and the question whether the hierarchy still collapses at exponent 3 remained open.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{WKL}_0^* + \mathsf{CRT}^2_2$ $\forall\Pi^0_4$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0^*$? Does $\mathsf{CRT}^2_2$ imply that the cut $\mathrm{I}^0_1$ is closed under exponentiation? Is $\mathsf{RCA}_0^* + \mathsf{CRT}^2_2$ polynomially simulated by $\mathsf{RCA}_0^*$ for $\forall\Pi_3$ sentences?
questions.answer: CRT²₂ implies that I⁰₁ is closed under exponentiation over RCA₀*, hence it has non-elementary proof speedup over RCA₀* for Π₁ sentences (so no polynomial simulation); ∀Π⁰₄-conservation is open.
questions.context: Over RCA₀*, the cohesive Ramsey theorem CRT²₂ behaves very differently from RT²₂ and CAC [@fioricaroneskoodziejczykkowalik2021]. Kowalik [@kowalik2025] showed that WKL₀* + CAC is polynomially simulated by RCA₀* for ∀Π⁰₃ sentences, in contrast with RT²₂. Kołodziejczyk and Sun [@kolodziejczyksun2026] showed that CRT²₂ makes the cut I⁰₁ exponentially closed, which gives a large speedup and shows that CRT²₂ is not provable from CAC over RCA₀*.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{BRT}^2_2$ $\Pi^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: BRT²₂ follows from RT²₂ [@lehoueroupatey2025], so a negative answer would show that RT²₂ is not Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂ — the long-standing question on the first-order part of Ramsey's theorem for pairs.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{HT}$ $\forall\Pi^0_3$-conservative over $\mathsf{ACA}_0$?
questions.context: Whether Hindman's theorem is provable in ACA₀ is open (see the question on Hindman's theorem). Le Houérou and Patey [@lehoueroupatey2026] suggest a weaker, first-order version of the question that the largeness techniques used for Ramsey's theorem might reach.

questions.question: Does the thin set theorem for pairs and three colors $\mathsf{TS}^2_3$ imply $\mathsf{EM}$? Does it imply $\mathsf{FS}^2$?
questions.context: TS²₂ is RT²₂, which implies EM, while Liu and Patey [@liupatey2022] showed that TS²₄ does not even imply the stable Erdős–Moser theorem, by preservation of 2-hyperimmunity. Three colors is the only case left. More generally, Cholak and Patey determined for which numbers of colors the thin set theorems admit cone avoidance [@dzhafarovmummert2022].

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RT}^1_4$ Weihrauch reducible to $\mathsf{ADS}$?
questions.context: Over RCA₀, ADS implies RT¹_{<∞} since it implies BΣ⁰₂. In the Weihrauch degrees, Fiori-Carones, Shafer and Soldà [@fioricaronesshafersolda2022] showed that RT¹₃ is strongly Weihrauch reducible to ADC (and so to ADS) but RT¹₅ is not Weihrauch reducible to ADS: four colors is the remaining case.

questions.question: The generalized Higman theorem (if $Q$ is a bqo then so is $Q^{<\omega}$) is provable in $\mathsf{ATR}_0$.
questions.context: Marcone [@marcone1994] proved GHT in Π¹₁-CA₀ and conjectured that ATR₀ suffices, as a step towards his conjecture that Nash-Williams' theorem is provable in ATR₀: over ATR₀, the two statements are closely tied. Montalbán [@montalban2011] recalls that they are equivalent over ATR₀.
